john.19.p1.b1.text: Then Pilate took Jesus and had Him flogged.

john.19.p1.b2.text: The soldiers twisted together a crown of thorns, set it on His head, and dressed Him in a purple robe.

john.19.p2.b1.text: Look, I am bringing Him out to you to let you know that I find no basis for a charge against Him.

john.19.p2.b2.text: When Jesus came out wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe,

john.19.p3.b2.text: You take Him and crucify Him, … for I find no basis for a charge against Him.

john.19.p3.b3.text: We have a law, … and according to that law He must die, because He declared Himself to be the Son of God.

john.19.p4.b1.text: When Pilate heard this statement, he was even more afraid, and he went back into the Praetorium. …

john.19.p4.b3.text: Do You not know that I have authority to release You and authority to crucify You?

john.19.p4.b4.text: You would have no authority over Me if it were not given to you from above.

john.19.p5.b1.text: From then on, Pilate tried to release Him,

john.19.p5.b2.text: If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who declares himself a king is defying Caesar.

john.19.p5.b3.text: When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus out and sat on the judgment seat at a place called the Stone Pavement, …

john.19.p6.b1.text: It was the day of Preparation for the Passover, about the sixth hour.

john.19.p6.b3.text: Away with Him! Away with Him! Crucify Him!

john.19.p6.b4.text: We have no king but Caesar,

john.19.p7.b1.text: Carrying His own cross, He went out

john.19.p7.b2.text: to The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.

john.19.p7.b3.text: There they crucified Him, and with Him two others, one on each side, with Jesus in the middle.

john.19.p8.b1.text: Pilate also had a notice posted on the cross. It read: JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.

john.19.p8.b2.text: Many of the Jews read this sign,

john.19.p8.b3.text: Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but only that He said, ‘I am the King of the Jews.’

john.19.p8.b4.text: What I have written, I have written.

john.19.p9.b1.text: When the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they divided His garments into four parts, one for each soldier,

john.19.p9.b2.text: It was seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom.

john.19.p9.b3.text: Let us not tear it. Instead, let us cast lots to see who will get it.

john.19.p9.b4.text: They divided My garments among them, and cast lots for My clothing.

john.19.p10.b1.text: Near the cross of Jesus stood His mother and her sister, as well as Mary the wife of Clopas and Mary Magdalene.

john.19.p10.b4.text: So from that hour, this disciple took her into his home.

john.19.p11.b1.text: After this, knowing that everything had now been accomplished, and to fulfill the Scripture, Jesus said,

john.19.p11.b3.text: A jar of sour wine was sitting there.

john.19.p11.b4.text: So they soaked a sponge in the wine, put it on a stalk of hyssop, and lifted it to His mouth.

john.19.p12.b1.text: When Jesus had received the sour wine, He said,

john.19.p12.b3.text: And bowing His head, He yielded up His spirit.

john.19.p13.b1.text: It was the day of Preparation, and the next day was a High Sabbath. In order that the bodies would not remain on the cross during the Sabbath, the Jews asked Pilate to have the legs broken and the bodies removed.

john.19.p13.b2.text: So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man who had been crucified with Jesus, and those of the other.

john.19.p13.b3.text: But when they came to Jesus and saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs.

john.19.p14.b1.text: Instead, one of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear, and immediately blood and water flowed out.

john.19.p14.b2.text: The one who saw it has testified to this, and his testimony is true. He knows that he is telling the truth, so that you also may believe.

john.19.p14.b3.text: Now these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled: “Not one of His bones will be broken.”

john.19.p14.b4.text: And, as another Scripture says: “They will look on the One they have pierced.”

john.19.p15.b1.text: Afterward, Joseph of Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus (but secretly for fear of the Jews),

john.19.p15.b2.text: asked Pilate to let him remove the body of Jesus.

john.19.p15.b3.text: Pilate gave him permission, so he came and removed His body.

john.19.p16.b1.text: Nicodemus, who had previously come to Jesus at night, also brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about seventy-five pounds.

john.19.p16.b2.text: So they took the body of Jesus and wrapped it in linen cloths with the spices, according to the Jewish burial custom.

john.19.p17.b1.text: Now there was a garden in the place where Jesus was crucified, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid.

john.19.p17.b2.text: And because it was the Jewish day of Preparation and the tomb was nearby, they placed Jesus there.
